card.name: Words just before a condition or procedure
card.fires_on: Small connecting words or pieces such as "with", "e.g.,", "post" and "and" that sit right before a named condition, procedure or trial group. Seen in drug-label indication and warning text.

modes.label: Post before operative terms
modes.description: The prefix "post" just before a hyphen and a surgery-related word like operative or tonsillectomy.
modes.example: the management of<< post>>-operative pain, including use after out-p

modes.label: Links before a condition
modes.description: Linking words or punctuation like "with" or "e.g.," that lead into a disease or pain condition.
modes.example: Nausea and Vomiting Associated<< with>> Chemotherapy in Adult Patients Who Failed Con

modes.label: Section numbers and trial groups
modes.description: A section number or "and" that precedes a cancer type or trial name.
modes.example: 2.<<2>> Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer For treatment

card.writes: It nudges the next word toward disease or procedure names such as cancer, benign, and surgery, and away from words like side effects and symptoms.
card.plain: It fires on small words that come right before the name of a disease or surgery in a drug label.
